component.name: hivemq
component.title: HiveMQ
component.description: Send messages to and receive messages from an MQTT broker with the HiveMQ MQTT Client.
component.label: messaging,iot

cleanStart.description: Whether to initiate a clean session upon connecting to the broker (called clean session in MQTT 3.1.1 and clean start in MQTT 5). The two protocol versions behave differently when this is false: with MQTT 3.1.1 the broker keeps the session (subscriptions and queued QoS 1/2 messages) indefinitely, while with MQTT 5 the session still expires on disconnect, since this component does not set a session expiry interval.

clientId.description: The MQTT client identifier. If not set, the broker assigns one to each connection, but with MQTT 3.1.1 the broker then rejects a connection with cleanStart false. Each consumer and each producer opens its own connection, and the broker disconnects a client when another one connects with the same identifier, so a set identifier must be unique per endpoint.

configuration.description: To use a shared HiveMQConfiguration with the default values of the options. Each endpoint uses a copy of it, in which the options of the endpoint replace its values.

host.description: The host name or IP address of the MQTT broker.

mqttVersion.description: The MQTT protocol version to use when connecting to the broker.

port.description: The TCP port of the MQTT broker. The port does not change when ssl is true: set it to the TLS port of the broker, usually 8883.

qos.description: The Quality of Service (QoS) level that the producer publishes with, and the maximum QoS of the subscription of the consumer. The CamelHiveMQQos header replaces it for the producer. The consumer acknowledges a QoS 1 or 2 message when it receives it, before the route processes it.

retained.description: Whether the producer publishes messages with the retain flag, so that the broker keeps the last message of the topic and sends it to new subscribers. The CamelHiveMQRetained header replaces it.

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

password.label: security
password.description: The password for MQTT simple authentication with the broker. It is sent only when username is set.

ssl.label: security
ssl.description: Whether to connect to the broker with TLS. The client uses the default trust store of the JVM and no client certificate. The port option does not change: set it to the TLS port of the broker, usually 8883.

username.label: security
username.description: The user name for MQTT simple authentication with the broker.

CamelHiveMQTopic.description: The topic of the received message, set by the consumer. With a wildcard subscription it is the actual topic name. The producer does not read this header: use CamelHiveMQOverrideTopic to publish to another topic.

CamelHiveMQQos.description: The QoS level of the message. The consumer sets the QoS that the message was delivered with, and the producer publishes with this value instead of the qos option.

CamelHiveMQRetained.description: Whether the retain flag of the message is set. The consumer sets it, true for a retained message that the broker sends for a new subscription, and the producer publishes with this value instead of the retained option.

CamelHiveMQOverrideTopic.description: The topic that the producer publishes to instead of the topic of the endpoint. toD sets it to the topic of its URI and removes it after the send, but keeps a header that is already set, which then replaces the topic of the toD URI.

consumerOut.description: The payload of the MQTT message, an empty byte array for an empty payload. The topic is in the CamelHiveMQTopic header

producerIn.description: What converts to a byte array: text, bytes, a stream or a file, sent as the payload; no body is sent as an empty payload. A Map, a POJO or a number does not convert and fails the exchange: marshal it first

topic.description: The MQTT topic. The consumer subscribes to it as a topic filter, which can contain the wildcards + and #. The producer publishes to it as a topic name without wildcards, and the CamelHiveMQOverrideTopic header replaces it.

exceptionHandler.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.
